forecast-period.text: A high pressure system south of SA extends a ridge over the state. A cold front is forecast to pass over the southeast early Tuesday, followed quickly by a high pressure system that is expected to pass over the south of the state later Tuesday and on Wednesday, maintaining a ridge over the state. Another cold front is expected to start moving across the Bight later in the week
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible morning fog in the far west. Mostly dry, though a slight chance of an isolated shower over the far north. Maximum temperatures below average. Light winds, tending northwesterly in the south during the day.
Showers over most districts, clearing in the west during the evening. Isolated thunderstorms possible in the northwest. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

Showers about the southern agricultural area, clearing during the day. Dry in the north. Maximum temperatures below average. Northwesterly winds in the south, tending south to southwesterly during the day and fresh about the southeast coast. South to southeasterly winds in the north.
Dry. Maximum temperatures below average in the east, gradient to above average in the west. Southeast to northeasterly winds.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms developing in the west during the day. Dry elsewhere. Maximum temperatures near average, tending above average in the west. Northeast to northwesterly winds, fresh in the west during the day.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Thursday: Less than 2 mm across the far northeast and agricultural areas, increasing to 2 to 5 mm in the Mount Lofty Ranges. 2 to 10 mm elsewhere, increasing to 10 to 15 mm in the North West Pastoral district.
